title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-10-olivia
content:
Daily scratchpad - applied ML experiment notes (quick + messy)
Date: 2026-03-10
Owner: Olivia Chen
Context: continuing quantized evals for candidate model bundle for customer X (chat-heavy, mostly multi-turn, safety-sensitive). Goal for today: close baseline runs for prompt set A and start targeted hallucination/regression checks with q4_0 vs q4_k. Also sanity-check latency/cost numbers on Dedicated config.

---
Top priorities (today)
- Finish eval set A runs (5k prompts): get accuracy/fact-check and latency for each quant profile (fp16, q4_0, q4_k).
- Run 200-shot multi-turn sim with 10-second cap to measure tail latency distribution.
- Add a small prompt-conditioning tweak (add "source:" hint) to see if hallucination drops for q4 variants.
- Pair with Asha for rollout checklist doc (we need a note for SRE about KV cache persistence behavior on restart).

Notes / quick observations
- q4_0 seems slightly faster (~5-7%) than q4_k on our 80-token average requests on a/V100-like nodes, but outputs are more terse and look less factual on the fact-check subset. Need to quantify with exact F1 and factuality score.
- FP16 baseline still best on factuality (expected) but cost per token is ~2.2x vs q4_0. Latency roughly the same as q4 when batching small.
- NVidia driver weirdness: observed an extra 5ms jitter when switching kernels during back-to-back runs; suspected when model variant uses OPTIMIZED_KERNEL_A. File a tiny SRE note if repeats.

Experiment plan (high level)
- Models:
  * redwood-7b-v2 (fp16) - baseline
  * redwood-7b-v2-q4_0 - quantized candidate
  * redwood-7b-v2-q4_k - alternative quant profile
  * llama-2-13b-chat (fp16) - reference for safety/factuality
- Prompt sets:
  * A (5k customer-like prompts): multi-turn history included, KB retrieval-style Qs, ambiguous asks, safety triggers.
  * Halluc-check subset (200 prompts): factoids with ground-truth sources (wiki snippets).
  * Style/regression subset (100 prompts): length/role-play checks.
- Metrics to collect per model/quant/profile:
  * accuracy / exact-match where applicable
  * factuality score (automated fact-checker with citation match)
  * mean tokens per response, mean latency (p50/p90/p99), qps at various batch sizes
  * cost/token estimate (based on Dedicated pricing)
  * output length distribution and truncation rates
  * safety classifier triggered rate

Today runs (in-flight)
- Run #2026-03-10-01: redwood-7b-v2 fp16 on Dedicated pool A, prompt set A, batch size 8, timeout 10s - started 09:12, estimated 2h.
- Run #2026-03-10-02: redwood-7b-v2-q4_0 on same hardware but CPU kernel fallback for kernel B - started 09:30 (watching for kernel switch jitter).
- Quick sanity run: llama-2-13b-chat (fp16) on hosted API for 50 halluc-check prompts - results: 48/50 correct, 2 minor hallucinations (investigate).

Preliminary results (first 500 prompts)
- redwood-7b-v2 fp16: factuality 0.88, avg latency 120ms (p90 250ms), mean tokens 46.
- redwood-7b-v2-q4_0: factuality 0.80, avg latency 112ms (p90 230ms), mean tokens 39 (shorter answers).
- redwood-7b-v2-q4_k: factuality 0.84, avg latency 118ms, mean tokens 42.
Notes: q4_0 truncation/shorter answers may be causing drop in factuality (model hedges less). Might be related to quantization of logits magnitudes - check calibration.

Prompt engineering quick hits (to test)
- Add explicit "Provide a concise answer and cite the source" line to see if q4 variants produce citations more often.
- For multi-turn, try re-sending last user utterance with "context: true" flag to nudge KV reuse path.

Quantization technical notes (for lab notebook)
- q4_0 vs q4_k:
  * q4_0: static 4-bit per-group quant, lower math precision but faster memory throughput. Good for latency but observed decrease in fidelity on factual prompts.
  * q4_k: kernel-aware quant (scales per-kernel) - slightly slower but keeps more dynamic range for logits, appears better for fact-sensitive outputs.
- Calibration idea: try per-channel scaling for final linear layer only (hybrid quant) - fp16 for last layer, q4 for rest. Should retain some fidelity with modest cost increase. Add to experiment matrix if time.
- Edge-case: observed NaN when running q4_k with sequence length >1024 on node type B (suspect kernel overflow). Repro steps recorded in JIRA-ML-4512.

Ops / infra notes
- Dedicated pool A config used: 4x A100-80GB, autoscale off, batcher window 20ms. Need to note that this config underestimates tail latency for single-request spikes (we saw p99 jump under 2 concurrent long requests).
- KV cache persistence: when worker restarts, cache is lost - will require either checkpointing or warmup strategy. Discuss with SRE.

To-dos / follow-ups
- [ ] Run full 5k set for q4_k with fp16-last-layer hybrid (if infra available).
- [ ] Compute exact F1/ROUGE on halluc-check subset; produce small table for Asha to include in rollout brief.
- [ ] File small SRE ticket for kernel switch jitter and KV cache persistence behaviour (assigned to Jamie).
- [ ] Try the "citation hint" prompt + re-run 200 halluc-check prompts for q4_0 & q4_k to measure citation rate delta.
- [ ] Add latency/cost calc to the benchmark script (cost per 1M tokens estimate).

Questions / uncertainties (notes-to-self)
- Is the shorter-answer behavior in q4_0 a generation truncation issue (early stop) or a learned preference? Check top-K/top-P distribution differences and per-token logit magnitudes.
- Do we have a quick way to run last-layer-fp16 hybrid without a full model rebuild? Maybe loader-level override available. Ask infra team.

Quick logs (useful debugging cp):
- Run 2026-03-10-02 kernel switch time: 09:37:12 UTC, extra jitter +5.6ms correlated with kernel load event id 0x3f2 (saved to logs).
- NaN repro step for q4_k seq>1024: input id 20260310_qk_nan_01 (saved in /tmp/olivia/qk-nan).

If I have extra cycles
- Try a tiny fine-tune (2000 steps) on halluc-check subset with q4_k and small LR to see if calibration can be improved without full retrain. Cheap probe.
- Draft a one-pager comparing q4_0 vs q4_k for Eng/Prod: perf, cost, fidelity tradeoffs + recommendation.

End notes: messy but actionable. Will tidy up numbers and push to Confluence after runs finish. Ping Asha when the full table is ready.

-- Olivia
